canonical_statement: For real-valued random variables X_n and Y_n on a common probability space, if X_n converges in distribution to Z and Y_n converges in probability to the constant c, then (X_n,Y_n), X_n+Y_n, and X_n*Y_n converge in distribution to (Z,c), Z+c, and Z*c; when c is nonzero, X_n/Y_n converges in distribution to Z/c.
domain_and_universes: universes u v w; index iota : Type u; common source Omega : Type v; limit source OmegaL : Type w; real-valued functions; Prop in universe 0
ordered_binders: mu : Measure Omega and IsProbabilityMeasure mu
muL : Measure OmegaL and IsProbabilityMeasure muL
hypotheses: TendstoInDistribution X l Z (fun _ => mu) muL
conclusion: Pair, sum, and product convergence in distribution, together with c != 0 implying quotient convergence in distribution.
